request: The earbuds are too large and bulky here. Make them smaller and more compact
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the supplied sculpture image. Change ONLY the visible earbud and its immediate fit: the earbud is currently too big and protrudes too much.

Make the entire earpiece approximately TWO THIRDS of its current width and height, and reduce the protruding housing depth by roughly HALF. It should feel small, discreet and closely nestled into the ear bowl, with more visible stone ear around it. Keep the ear itself exactly the same size. The faceplate must sit close to the ear rather than on a thick projecting cylindrical body.

Preserve the CYMBA design: small rounded satin graphite faceplate, very fine champagne rim, a slim smoky dark inner housing, compact black silicone support wing tucked naturally into the upper concha, hidden ear tip, and a fine black braided cable exiting downward. Reduce the wing proportionately, avoiding a large protruding fin. Make the cable and its strain relief slightly more delicate to suit the smaller body. Keep the same natural downward cable route beside the neck. Maintain convincing perspective, contact shadows and realistic physical fit.

The smaller device should reveal a little more of the pink ear-area neural pathway beside/behind the housing. Keep nerves separate from the cable and never paint them across the faceplate.

Everything else must remain unchanged: exact marble sculpture, head and neck size, pose, face, blank carved eyes, white stone texture, transparent rear shell, complete pink/purple network, lighting, framing and composition. Do not make the whole sculpture smaller, zoom out, rotate it or change the pathway. No additional objects, anatomy, labels, text or background. Preserve genuine transparent alpha.
